record.paper_title: Causal Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning: Review and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Beyond graphical SCMs in causal MARL
record.original_question: How should causal MARL research incorporate causal modeling approaches beyond graphical structural causal models, such as potential outcomes, propensity scores, instrumental variables, and relationships between differential equations and causal models, while preserving the benefits of explicit causal assumptions for MARL?

evidence.quote: The authors would like to point out that causal modelling approaches are not limited to graphical model literature, though we have mostly focused on these here as graphical methods are well suited to current approaches to computational sciences in addition to being easy to understand.

There exists extensive literature on potential outcomes and propensity scores (Rubin, 2005; Rosenbaum and Rubin, 1983). Instrumental variable (Becker, 2016) approaches are very common in practice, recently extended as a basis for CRL (Li et al., 2021).
We also make note of relationships between differential equations and causal models, which are investigated in various settings (Mooij et al., 2013; Bongers and Mooij, 2018; Schölkopf, 2019).

artifact.status_search_result: This is posed as an open research direction asking for the development of causal MARL frameworks that go beyond graphical SCMs to incorporate potential outcomes, propensity scores, instrumental variables, or differential-equation-based causal models. Web search reveals ongoing work on causal RL with IVs and on potential-outcomes-based off-policy evaluation, but no comprehensive multi-agent framework that integrates these paradigms with identifiability and algorithmic guarantees. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Causal Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning: Review and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Open problems include extending causal MARL beyond graphical SCM approaches.
status_evidence.claim: The question is explicitly framed as an open problem in causal MARL.
